newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus posts year A$60 mln profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus posts year A$60 mln profit.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd, Australia's second largest telecommunications group, said on Wednesday it achieved a pre-tax profit of A$60.3 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
The result compared to a loss of A$17.0 million in 1994/95.
Optus said total revenue rose 36 percent to A$1.94 billion during 1995/96 while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation jumped 130 percent to A$456 million.

Chief executive Zygmunt Switkowski said Optus achieved its first full year profit on the back of an increase in revenue across all lines of business and a strong improvement in margins. "The profit ... reflected both business growth and the benefits of size as Optus carried more and more traffic on its own network," he said in a statement.
Business Network Services sales grew 59 percent to A$233.0 million, while the total number of Optus Mobile customers, both analogue and digital, increased 66 percent.
The number of Optus Mobile Digital customers increased 246 percent.
Optus Mobile Digital services use Optus' own mobile network.

Switkowski said that since the start of the calendar year, Mobile Digital customers accounted for nearly 80 percent of the net additions in Optus Mobile customers. This trend was expected to continue with the federal government's recent confirmation that it planned to shut down the analogue network by 2000.
Optus Long Distance recorded further growth in both national and international traffic with over 1.6 million customers increasing Optus' share of the total long distance market to 16 percent.
Payments for connections to other networks reduced to 34 percent of revenue as more calls were carried on the Optus network. This compared to 40 percent of revenue last year.

Optus shareholders include Mayne Nickless Ltd, BellSouth Corp, and Cable and Wireless Plc, which each hold about one-quarter of the company. Institutions hold the remainder. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
